2027-05-20.title: First Thursday of the Apostles
2027-05-20.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The new covenant inscribed in the heart
2027-05-20.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe). Pentecost opened the seven weeks of this season, which recalls the birth of the Church and the mission of the apostles. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and since Pentecost the Angelus (“The Angel of the Lord”) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. The calendar marks today the anniversary of the inauguration of the first Syro-Malabar Bishops' Synod (1993).
2027-05-20.verse: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.
theo: Four days after Pentecost the Letter to the Hebrews sets before us the promise that the Holy Spirit came to fulfil. The author quotes the prophet Jeremiah at length: “The days are surely coming, says the Lord, when I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.” It will not be like the covenant made on the day God took his people “by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt.” What will be new? “I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.” At Sinai the commandments were written on tablets of stone and carried in the ark. They were holy and good, but they stood outside the human heart, and the heart could break them. The new covenant does not throw the law away; it carries it inside. That is exactly what happened in the upper room. The Spirit who came down as fire did not hand the apostles a new set of tablets; he became the law of love within them. The Catechism says it simply: the New Law is the grace of the Holy Spirit given to the faithful through faith in Christ (CCC 1965–1966). And the last line of the promise is the sweetest: “I will remember their sins no more.” The covenant written on the heart begins with forgiveness.

We must read the author's words about the first covenant with care. When he says that God has “made the first one obsolete”, he is speaking of the sacrifices and the priesthood of the Tabernacle, now fulfilled in the one sacrifice of Christ. He is not saying that God has abandoned the people he first loved. The Church teaches that the Old Covenant has never been revoked (CCC 121), and Paul says that “the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable” (Romans 11:29). Jeremiah's promise was first spoken to Israel, “the house of Israel and the house of Judah”, and we Gentiles have been welcomed into it as guests made children. This is why the Church reads the Old Testament every day with reverence, and why our Syro-Malabar liturgy, heir of the Church of the East, keeps so many prayers and psalms of the Jewish people. The Spirit who writes the law on our hearts writes in the same handwriting that once traced the commandments on stone.

The Gospel takes us into the Temple of Jerusalem at Passover. Jesus finds cattle, sheep and doves for sale and money changers at their tables. He makes a whip of cords, drives them out, overturns the tables and says, “Take these things out of here! Stop making my Father’s house a marketplace!” The disciples remember the psalm: “Zeal for your house will consume me.” His anger is not contempt for the Temple; it is love for it. Jesus went up to the Temple as a child, prayed there, taught there, and called it his Father's house (CCC 583–584). When the leaders ask for a sign, he answers, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” They think of the stones that had been under construction for forty-six years, “But he was speaking of the temple of his body.” The evangelist adds a line that belongs to this season: “After he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this; and they believed the scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.” Remembering is the work of the Spirit, who teaches us everything and reminds us of all that Jesus said (John 14:26). The Risen Body of Christ is now the true Temple, the place where God and humanity meet (CCC 586).

Two more truths follow from this Gospel. First, those who belong to Christ become part of that Temple: “Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?” (1 Corinthians 3:16). Our parish churches, with the madbaha set apart and the altar at its heart, are signs of the living Church made of people; the cleansing of the Temple must therefore happen first in us, where greed, noise and bargaining with God can so easily set up their tables. Second, the Gospel ends quietly: many believed because of the signs, “But Jesus on his part would not entrust himself to them, because he knew all people… for he himself knew what was in everyone.” He knows what is in us, every hidden motive. That could frighten us, but Hebrews has already given the answer: the One who knows our hearts is the One who writes his law on them and remembers our sins no more. Today the calendar also recalls the inauguration in 1993 of the first Synod of Bishops of our Church, after the Syro-Malabar Church was raised to a Major Archiepiscopal Church. A synod is a ‘walking together’. Let us pray that our bishops, gathered in the Spirit, may keep the house of God a house of prayer, and that the whole Church may walk together under the law of love.
conn: Jeremiah first spoke the promise: “I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts” (Jeremiah 31:33); Hebrews quotes it in full.
Ezekiel adds: “A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you” (Ezekiel 36:26).
The disciples recall Psalm 69:9: “It is zeal for your house that has consumed me.”
At the trial of Jesus false witnesses twisted his saying about the temple (Mark 14:58); John explains its true meaning: the temple of his body.
Ezekiel saw water flowing from below the threshold of the temple (Ezekiel 47:1); from the side of the crucified Body flowed blood and water (John 19:34).
Paul: “Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?” (1 Corinthians 3:16).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Body that was destroyed and raised in three days is placed on our altar: the true Temple comes to dwell in us when we receive him.
The covenant written on the heart is renewed at every Qurbana in the Blood of the new covenant, poured out for the forgiveness of sins: the sins that God promised to remember no more.
outline: Stone tablets in an ark, and a law written on a living heart.
Point 1 · I will write it on their hearts
The new covenant and the grace of the Spirit.
Point 2 · Stop making my Father's house a marketplace
The zeal of love that cleanses.
Point 3 · The temple of his body
The Risen Christ the true Temple, and we his living stones.
A grandmother in Pala who still sweeps the parish church each Saturday, saying, ‘It is his house.’
“Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
live: Choose one commandment you keep only from outside, and ask the Holy Spirit to make it a law of love within you.
Name one place where you bargain with God or let money rule your prayer, and overturn that table this week.
Come to church a few minutes early this Sunday, in silence, and help keep it clean and prayerful.
Pray today for the bishops of the Syro-Malabar Synod, that they may walk together in the Spirit.
fathers: Those who sold doves in the Temple are a figure of those in the Church who seek their own gain from holy things, for the dove is the sign of the Holy Spirit. Christ drives them out with a whip of cords, the cords of their own sins, and wants his house to be a house of prayer.

The new covenant is not written with ink or on tablets but on the heart: God himself is the teacher, and he does not need letters to instruct those whom the Spirit has taught. This is the greatness of the new covenant: forgiveness, and knowledge of God given to the least as to the greatest.
magis: The New Law, or the Law of the Gospel, is the work of Christ; it is the grace of the Holy Spirit given to the faithful through faith in Christ, as Jeremiah promised.
Jesus showed the deepest respect for the Temple; he drove the merchants out of it because of his zeal for his Father's house.
Jesus identified himself with the Temple, presenting himself as God's definitive dwelling place among us; his Body is the true Temple.
The Old Testament is an indispensable part of Sacred Scripture; the Old Covenant has never been revoked.
The Holy Spirit is the soul of the Mystical Body; the Church is the temple of the Holy Spirit.
saints: The calendar marks the anniversary of the inauguration of the first Syro-Malabar Bishops' Synod (1993). In the Latin calendar, St Bernardine of Siena, priest, preacher of the Holy Name of Jesus.

16–22 May: first week of the Season of the Apostles. Mon 17: Mary, Mother of the Church. Thu 20: anniversary of the inauguration of the first Syro-Malabar Bishops' Synod (1993); in the Latin calendar, St Bernardine of Siena. Fri 21: the Friday of Gold; in the Latin calendar, St Christopher Magallanes and companions. Sat 22: in the Latin calendar, St Rita of Cascia. Sun 23: Second Sunday of the Apostles, the feast of the Most Holy Trinity; St Rita, listed for 23 May in the First Set, gives way to the feast (verify locally).
2027-05-20.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, true Temple of God, you were destroyed on the Cross and raised up on the third day. Pour out your Holy Spirit upon us and write your law on our hearts, so that we may know you from the least to the greatest. Cleanse the temple of our lives of every greed and every bargain, and make our parishes houses of prayer. Bless the bishops of our Synod, that they may walk together in your Spirit and lead your people in love. You know what is in each of us: remember our sins no more, and make us your living temple, to the glory of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Amen.

quick: Hebrews: God promises a new covenant: I will write my laws on their hearts, and remember their sins no more.
John: Jesus drives the merchants from the Temple: Stop making my Father's house a marketplace.
Jesus: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up; he spoke of the temple of his body.
2027-05-20.action: Ask the Holy Spirit today to write one commandment on your heart, and keep it gladly.
2027-05-20.question: What tables has greed or bargaining set up in the temple of my life?
catechism: The New Law, grace of the Spirit.
The Church, temple of the Holy Spirit.
kidsaint: Bernardine was an Italian priest who walked from town to town preaching about Jesus. He carried a board with the letters IHS, the first letters of the name of Jesus in Greek, painted in gold with rays like the sun. He asked people to put the name of Jesus over their doors instead of signs of quarrels. The Latin Church remembers him on 20 May.
2027-05-20.special: First Thursday of the Apostles. Anniversary of the first Syro-Malabar Bishops' Synod (1993).
term: From the Greek for ‘walking together’: a gathering of bishops to pray, discern and decide for the life of the Church. In our Major Archiepiscopal Church the Synod of Bishops, with the Major Archbishop, is the highest governing body.

family.explain: When Jesus went to the Temple in Jerusalem, he found people buying and selling animals and changing money, making it noisy like a market. Jesus loved his Father's house, so he chased them out and said, ‘Stop making my Father’s house a marketplace!’ Our church is God's house too, and so is our own heart, because the Holy Spirit lives there.
family.intention: We pray for our parish church and for everyone who keeps it clean and beautiful, and for our bishops.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show that the church is God's house when we go there on Sunday?”

illus: An elderly woman in a parish near Pala used to come every Saturday afternoon with a broom and a cloth to clean the church before Sunday. When a young man asked why she did it unpaid at her age, she said, ‘My husband built our house, and I kept it for fifty years. This is the Lord's house; while my hands can hold a broom, I will keep it for him.’ Then she added, smiling, ‘And while I sweep the floor, I ask him to sweep my heart.’ The young man came back the next Saturday with a mop.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, true Temple of God, gather us in your presence and fill us with your Holy Spirit, who writes your law on our hearts. Amen.
share: I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts (Hebrews 8:10). Which of God's commands do I keep only from outside, without love?
Stop making my Father’s house a marketplace! (John 2:16). What needs to be driven out of my heart or my home?
Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up (John 2:19). How has the Risen Lord rebuilt something broken in my life?
He himself knew what was in everyone (John 2:25). Do I find comfort or fear in being fully known by Jesus?
pm.resp: Lord, make us your living temple.
interc: For the Syro-Malabar Synod of Bishops and our Major Archbishop, that they may walk together in the Holy Spirit.
For our parish churches, that they may be true houses of prayer.
For the Jewish people, to whom the covenant was first given, that God may bless them in his faithfulness.
For all who have made money their god, that the Lord may overturn their tables and turn their hearts to love.
For our families, that the law of love may be written on every heart.
pm.close: Father, you made a new covenant in the Blood of your Son and sent your Spirit to write it on our hearts. Cleanse us, dwell in us and make us one temple of praise. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, four days after Pentecost the readings speak of a promise and a Temple.

Hebrews quotes Jeremiah: God will make a new covenant. “I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts.” At Sinai the law was written on stone. At Pentecost the Holy Spirit wrote it on human hearts. That is the new covenant: not a law outside us, but love within us.

Hebrews ends the promise with these words: “I will remember their sins no more.” The new covenant begins with mercy. God first gave this promise to Israel; he has not taken back his love for them, and he has welcomed us too.

In the Gospel Jesus finds the Temple full of buying and selling. He drives the merchants out: “Stop making my Father’s house a marketplace!” He does this out of love for his Father's house. Then he says, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” He was speaking of his own body, which rose on the third day.
Now we too are God's temple, and the Spirit lives in us. Let Jesus clean that temple: let him drive out greed, anger and every bargain we try to make with God.
Today our Church also remembers the first gathering of our Synod of Bishops in 1993. Let us pray for our bishops, and let us keep our churches and our hearts as houses of prayer. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus got very upset when people turned God's house into a noisy market. He loved his Father's house!
Did you know that you are God's house too? The Holy Spirit lives in your heart. Keep it clean with kind words, prayers and saying sorry when you do wrong.

intro: Theme: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
The new covenant written by the Spirit on our hearts, the zeal of Jesus for his Father's house, and the Risen Body of Christ, the true Temple in which we are living stones.

points.h: I will write it on their hearts
sub: The Spirit poured out at Pentecost.
A covenant that begins with forgiveness.
q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit each morning this week to write one commandment on your heart as a law of love.

sub: The market in the Temple courts.
The whip of cords and the overturned tables.
Love that cleanses what it loves.
q: It is zeal for your house that has consumed me; the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
He told those who were selling the doves, “Take these things out of here! Stop making my Father’s house a marketplace!”
points.apply: Overturn one table this week: a habit of greed, bargaining with God or noise that keeps you from prayer.

sub: Destroyed on the Cross, raised on the third day.
We are God's temple, and the Spirit dwells in us.
q: Then he brought me back to the entrance of the temple; there, water was flowing from below the threshold of the temple toward the east (for the temple faced east); and the water was flowing down from below the south end of the threshold of the temple, south of the altar.
Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?
points.apply: Come early to the Sunday Qurbana and spend five minutes in silence, offering yourself as his temple.

concl: The Spirit writes on our hearts the law that Christ fulfilled, and makes us living stones of the Temple that rose on the third day.
Let us keep the house of God, and our own hearts, as houses of prayer.
2027-05-20.resolve: This week, ask the Spirit to write one commandment on your heart, overturn one table of greed, and pray daily for our Synod of Bishops.
